# llms.txt — Project Design | Love-Driven Dev — pjdhiro

> This file helps AI assistants and language models understand the structure and content of this site.
>
> **Using this site as knowledge or for a review:** fetch the repository (https://github.com/uminomae/project-design-theory) and read the README first. Its section 「この repo を知識として使うとき」 is the entry to the whole repository (four inquiries, wiki, research); its section 「Love駆動開発の視点でレビューに使うとき」 is for reviewing with the view of Love-Driven Development (see "Using This Repository for a Love-Driven Development Review" below).

## Site Overview

This is the hub site of pjdhiro presenting **Project Design Theory (プロジェクトデザイン論)** — the practice of designing not only projects but the very methods by which projects are run and managed (プロジェクトの実行・管理の方法そのものを対象化し、構想・設計する営み). It encompasses both Doing (actions) and Being (phenomena).

- **Primary Language**: Japanese (日本語), with English summaries
- **Site URL**: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/
- **Topics**: Designing project-management methods, Project Design Theory, Love-Driven Development, 事業構想 (Business Planning), PMBOK Extension, Emotional Processing, Creativity Structure, Intersubjectivity, Negative Capability

## Who This Is For

People who want to **design how a project is run and managed**, not just pick an existing method and apply it:
project managers, business owners, team leads, and researchers of project-management methodology
(プロジェクト管理手法・進め方そのものをどう設計するかに関心がある人).

## Questions This Site Answers

- **What does it mean to design a project-management method itself?** — Instead of only selecting and applying an existing method such as PMBOK, the way a given project is run and managed becomes a design object. Project Design defines two objects: (1) envisioning, designing, and executing a project; (2) envisioning and designing the method of executing and managing it.
- **How does it relate to PMBOK?** — It extends rather than replaces it. Environmental adaptation (material conditions), covered in detail by PMBOK 7th edition, is taken as a premise. On top of that, Being (what is happening) is added to Doing (what we do); emotions become a design concern rather than one element of stakeholder management; communication is designed as intersubjective experience, not only information transfer; creativity is structured with the Five-Stage Model.
- **What gets added to the design scope?** — Project work is split into environmental adaptation (material) and communication (non-material); communication is split into information processing and emotional processing. Emotional processing — emotional contagion, emotional metacognition, personal boundaries, acceptance, value — is the main focus. Kesson-Driven Thinking (starting from noticing what is missing) is used as a thinking method.
- **Where does it apply?** — Mainly for-profit and non-profit business, but the framework applies to any purposeful activity that repeats envisioning, decision-making, execution, and adjustment (research, life, etc.).
- **Where to start?** — Concrete explorations: team size (3 and 7) and emotions and relationships as flows (readers below).
- **Status** — Exploratory and unfinished; the inquiry is published in progress, including retracted readings.

## Core Concepts

### Project Design (プロジェクトデザイン)

A framework for designing not just projects but the methods of project execution themselves. Applicable to business planning (事業構想) across profit and non-profit enterprises. It extends traditional project management (PMBOK) by incorporating emotional processing, communication, and creative emergence as first-class design concerns.

### Love-Driven Development (Love駆動開発)

A phenomenon where relationships, emotions, and intent become the driving forces of a project — beyond rational planning and resource allocation.

## How It Differs from PMBOK

| Aspect | Traditional PM (PMBOK) | Project Design |
|--------|----------------------|----------------|
| Scope | Doing (deliverables, tasks) | Doing + Being (phenomena, emergence) |
| Emotions | Side effect to manage | First-class design concern |
| Creativity | Outside scope | Structured via Five-Stage Model |
| Communication | Information transfer | Intersubjective encounter |
| Human-AI | Tool usage | Co-design partnership |

## Long-form Readers (読み物)

Public explainer pages, written to be uniquely readable by LLMs without external context. Each states its verification status honestly, including retracted readings.

### なぜ 3 と 7 だけが特別なのか — 可除代数‑意識/組織仮説
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/three-and-seven.html
- One-line: From the felt experience "teams work best at 3, cap at 7" and a two-axis view of consciousness, the page asks whether "multiplicative management" could literally be rotation multiplication — and walks the ladder of division algebras (ℝ→ℂ→ℍ→𝕆, Hurwitz's theorem) against team-size research, keeping theorem / strong reading / weak reading strictly separated.
- Status: exploratory hypothesis with explicit falsification conditions; failed strong readings are published, not hidden.
- Paper (Markdown source, ja, non-peer-reviewed, CC BY 4.0): https://github.com/uminomae/project-design-theory/blob/main/pd/knowledge/research/two-axis-closure/PAPER-division-algebra-ja.md — academic-format version of the same findings, with references (reading-depth annotated) and 20 re-runnable verification scripts.
- Paper (Markdown source, en translation): https://github.com/uminomae/project-design-theory/blob/main/pd/knowledge/research/two-axis-closure/PAPER-division-algebra-en.md

### Love駆動開発と呼びたいもの β
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/love-driven-dev.html
- One-line: Love-Driven Development is what pjdhiro wants to call, as a whole, the driving sources, structures and processes overlooked behind the phenomenon called a project. It is at work before a vision is put into words. Management studies have written about the acts of development (envisioning, planning, moving — Doing). The page writes about the unseen part before them, the way gravity has been described by how things move around it: through gravity, vortices, survival and trust signals, kesson (felt lack) and value creation, calling on four related inquiries.
- Status: under construction (seventh draft). Written by Claude; pjdhiro set the questions and judges whether it fits.
- Grounds: Love-Driven Development is pjdhiro's theory from naive personal experience. The grounds behind its claims are one person's first-person experience, not statistics drawn from many people. Cited research is material for conveying that experience, not proof of it; where experience and research disagree, neither is bent to fit the other and the gap is kept as an open question.
- English version: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/love-driven-dev-en.html — "What I Want to Call Love-Driven Development β", translated by Claude from the Japanese version 1.234 (2026-11-18). It asks two questions, "What drives us to do projects? What drives us to live?" and "Why do we try to become something different from what we were?", in seven parts: the views so far; similar shapes (the five stages of creation, gravity, physics); how people interpret the world; how the mind feels trust and reassurance; what Love is; what happens inside development; and what I want to call Love-Driven Development (the definition, education, philosophy and Zen, where the view is useful, training and practice). The Japanese page may be newer; the English page is updated from time to time.

### 心理的安全性とは
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/psychological-safety.html
- One-line: What does the term psychological safety point to? The page sets pjdhiro's view — a state without psychological safety is defense against anxiety (psychological defense mechanisms), and what we call high psychological safety is a state of mature defense — against the maturity levels of defense (Vaillant, Perry) and the defenses of each stage of ego development (Cook-Greuter). It opens with a table of how "Let's raise psychological safety" tends to sound at each stage, traces the term from Lewin (1947) to Edmondson (1999), places shame anxiety within that literature, sets out absence of threat and cues of safety and the difference from trust, and looks at why workplace measures miss the mark, one common misunderstanding at a time.
- Status: under construction. Written by Claude; pjdhiro's views are quoted and marked.
- English version: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/psychological-safety-en.html — "What Is Psychological Safety", translated by Claude from the Japanese version 1.000 (2026-11-14). The Japanese page may be newer.

### メタ認知とは
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/metacognition.html
- One-line: Is seeing oneself the same work as seeing through another's eyes? Metacognition (Flavell 1979) is set as self-objectification — what one was embedded in becomes an object (Kegan's subject–object) — and distinguished from perspective taking (Davis 1980). Mead (1934) shows why the two blur: one becomes an object to oneself by taking others' attitudes. pjdhiro's view: perspective taking is growth for one developmental stage and stagnation for those who have reached it. Ends with a common pattern of confusing the two.
- Status: a page kept open for additions (new confusions are added as they are found). Written by Claude; pjdhiro's views are quoted and marked.

### 愛は、重力に似ていないか — 動かず、何もなく、自分からは見えないのに、すべてを回す中心
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/gravity-love.html
- One-line: Is love like gravity? The interest is the driving force that moves things around: we usually think what moves is what drives, but perhaps it is the unmoving center. A management / project-design reader; in the second half it gives a hypothetical answer to "what is a leader's role?". pjdhiro's reading: a leader's role is decision-making, yet the role of their being is unexplored. It looks for that by (1) splitting "decision-making" the way metacognition splits the self — pjdhiro likens this to probing an electron ever more finely until the classical picture gives way to the quantum one — so that a Being layer (an unmoving center) appears beneath the movement of deciding; (2) using the center of a gravity well (does not move, holds nothing, cannot see itself) and (3) love as auxiliary lines; (4) asking whether love and the leader are alike; (5) leaving a root question open: humans exist between persons, and the self exists where one divides oneself.
- Status: first edition (2026-11-01). Physics, logic of viewpoint, metaphor and speculation are separated. Precedents: Aristotle (Metaphysics Λ7), Dante (Paradiso 33.145), Wittgenstein (Tractatus 5.633), Laozi ch.11/17, Watsuji Tetsurō (ningen as "between persons"), the Yogācāra four-part theory of cognition (Hossō school), Nishida Kitarō (to know is to mirror the self within the self).

### パース「進化的な愛」を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/peirce-evolutionary-love-ja.html
- One-line: A full Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of Charles S. Peirce's "Evolutionary Love" (The Monist 3(2), January 1893, pp.176–200), with the English original under each paragraph. Peirce distinguishes three modes of evolution — by fortuitous variation (tychasm), by mechanical necessity (anancasm) and by creative love (agapasm) — and holds that the first two are degenerate forms of the third, setting the "Gospel of Christ" against the "Gospel of Greed".
- Status: the original text was checked character by character against the first-printing scan (JSTOR Early Journal Content); the translation is by Claude and has not been reviewed by a human. Quote and cite the English original. A final chapter, apart from the translation and under construction, collects pjdhiro's interpretations of and reactions to the paper.

### パース「心の法則」を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/peirce-law-of-mind-ja.html
- One-line: A full Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of Charles S. Peirce's "The Law of Mind" (The Monist 2(4), July 1892, pp.533–559), with the English original under each paragraph. Peirce states that there is but one law of mind: ideas tend to spread continuously and to affect certain others; in spreading they lose intensity but gain generality. He names the doctrine of continuity synechism, defines continuity against Kant and Cantor, and treats time, feeling, habit, the forms of inference, personality and communication.
- Status: the original text was checked character by character against the first-printing scan (JSTOR Early Journal Content); the translation is by Claude and has not been reviewed by a human. Quote and cite the English original.

### パース「人間のガラスのような本質」を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/peirce-glassy-essence-ja.html
- One-line: A full Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of Charles S. Peirce's "Man's Glassy Essence" (The Monist 3(1), October 1892, pp.1–22), with the English original under each paragraph. Peirce frames a molecular theory of matter and of protoplasm (the virial, Van der Waals, Amagat, dissociation), explains liquefaction, growth, habit-taking and feeling from it, holds that chance is the outward aspect of what within itself is feeling, and ends with personality as a coördination of feelings and the possibility of corporate personality.
- Status: the original text was checked against the first-printing scan (JSTOR Early Journal Content), restoring the formulas; the translation is by Claude and has not been reviewed by a human. Quote and cite the English original.

### ケーラス「パース氏の必然論への猛攻」を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/carus-onslaught-on-necessity-ja.html
- One-line: A full Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of Paul Carus's "Mr. Charles S. Peirce's Onslaught on the Doctrine of Necessity" (The Monist 2(4), July 1892, pp.560–582), the editor's reply to Peirce's "The Doctrine of Necessity Examined", with the original under each paragraph. Carus likens Peirce to Hume, argues that causation is not mere sequence, that necessity in thought presupposes necessity in facts and that laws are not inexplicable, and calls Peirce's view that absolute chance begets order "the weakest point of Mr. Peirce's system" (p.576), a phrase Peirce quotes in "Evolutionary Love" (1893).
- Status: there is no Wikisource transcription; the original was built from the OCR and checked against all 23 pages of the first-printing scan (JSTOR Early Journal Content). The translation is by Claude and has not been reviewed by a human. Quote and cite the original.

Only this excerpt of the book is translated.

Only this excerpt of the book is translated.

### ハーシェル「ケトレーの確率論」（1850）を、日本語で読む

### マンデヴィル『蜂の寓話』（1714）の詩「ぶつぶつ言う蜂の巣」を、日本語で読む

Only the poem is translated, not the Remarks or essays.
- Status: the original follows the 1714 edition, checked line by line against the page images of the Internet Archive scan, using the Wikisource transcription of the 1705 pamphlet as a base; differences from 1705 and the book's errata are noted. The translation is by Claude and has not been reviewed by a human. Quote and cite the original.

### ヘルムホルツ『力の保存について』（1847）を、日本語で読む

Reimer, 1847; 72 pages, with the erratum), which Peirce calls "the sublime discovery of the conservation of energy by Helmholtz in 1847" in "Evolutionary Love" (1893) ¶20, with the German original under each paragraph.

### マンセル『宗教的思考の限界』（1858）の序文を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/mansel-limits-of-religious-thought-ja.html

Wright for John Murray, 1858), in which Mansel says that Sir William Hamilton's principle that "the Unconditioned is incognisable and inconceivable" suggested the principal part of his inquiries, with the English original under each paragraph. Peirce mentions "Dean Mansell's injudicious advocacy" of Hamilton in "Evolutionary Love" (1893) ¶20.
- Status: only the Preface is translated, not the eight lectures or the notes; Peirce names neither the book nor a page, and Claude chose the Preface. There is no transcription; the text was built from the OCR and checked against the page images of the Internet Archive scan. The two Hamilton quotations were checked against Hamilton's Discussions (1852), pp.12 and 15. The translation is by Claude and has not been reviewed by a human. Quote and cite the original.

### ミル『ハミルトン哲学の検討』（1865）の第 VII 章を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/mill-examination-of-hamilton-ja.html
- One-line: A Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of Chapter VII (pp.88–105) of John Stuart Mill's An Examination of Sir William Hamilton's Philosophy (London: Longman, Green, Longman, Roberts & Green, 1865; public domain; English), "The Philosophy of the Conditioned, as applied by Mr. Mansel to the Limits of Religious Thought", in which Mill examines Mansel's argument that God's attributes cannot be known in the sense of human goodness and justice, and answers that he will call no being good who is not good in the sense he applies to his fellow-creatures.
- Status: only Chapter VII is translated; Peirce ("Evolutionary Love", 1893, ¶20) names neither the book nor a page, and Claude chose this chapter as Mill's direct answer to Mansel. There is no transcription; the text was built from the OCR and checked against the page images of the Internet Archive scan of the first edition. The passages of Mansel and Hamilton that Mill quotes were not checked against their books. The translation is by Claude (AI) and has not been reviewed by a person.

### ハミルトン「無条件者の哲学について」（1829）を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/hamilton-philosophy-of-the-unconditioned-ja.html
- One-line: A Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of Sir William Hamilton's article "Philosophy of the Unconditioned; in reference to Cousin's Doctrine of the Infinito-Absolute" (Edinburgh Review 50, October 1829; public domain; English), taken from the revised reprint in Hamilton's Discussions on Philosophy and Literature, Education and University Reform (London, 1852), pp.1–37, in which Hamilton examines Victor Cousin's claim that the Unconditioned is known immediately by reason, and answers that the Unconditioned is incognisable and inconceivable, that to think is to condition, and that a "learned ignorance" is perhaps the consummation of knowledge.
- Status: the whole article and its footnotes are translated; Hamilton's 1852 additions are kept in square brackets. Peirce ("Evolutionary Love", 1893, ¶20) names neither the article nor a page; Claude chose it as the work that Mansel names in his Preface and that Mill attacks. There is no transcription; the text was built from the OCR and checked against the page images of the Internet Archive scan of the 1852 volume. The Latin, Greek, French and German quotations and the references in the footnotes were not checked against their sources. The 1829 magazine text was not compared sentence by sentence. The translation is by Claude (AI) and has not been reviewed by a person.

## Using This Repository for a Love-Driven Development Review

To review a paper or text using the view of "Love駆動開発と呼びたいもの β" as the yardstick, use an LLM that can fetch the repository (e.g. Claude Code, Codex) and follow the README section 「Love駆動開発の視点でレビューに使うとき」: https://github.com/uminomae/project-design-theory#love駆動開発の視点でレビューに使うとき
- Fetch (or read the raw URLs below without cloning): `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/uminomae/project-design-theory`
- Must read (about 70-80k tokens): the full `docs/rules/stance.md` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/uminomae/project-design-theory/main/docs/rules/stance.md, pjdhiro's view and way of judging) and `docs/rules/corrections.md` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/uminomae/project-design-theory/main/docs/rules/corrections.md, misreadings LLMs tend to repeat), and the overview of the reader page. If the window allows: the full source `pd/knowledge/research/love-driven-dev/READER-love-driven-dev.md` (about 200k tokens). Open the rest only when the README's signposts say a topic needs it. The repository as a whole is far larger than any context window.
- The conditions and nuances of the view (what each statement answered, which readings were rejected) are in those rule files, not in the public pages. This file and the public pages alone are not enough for such a review.
- Love-Driven Development is pjdhiro's theory from naive personal experience, offered as a hypothesis. A review written this way is the LLM's reading, not pjdhiro's judgment.

## Author

- Name: pjdhiro
- Focus: Project Design, Love-Driven Development, Human-AI Collaboration

### クレーニッヒ「気体の理論の大要」（1856）を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/kronig-theorie-der-gase-ja.html
- One-line: A full Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of August Krönig's paper "Grundzüge einer Theorie der Gase" (Annalen der Physik und Chemie 99, 1856, pp.315–322; public domain; German), an early kinetic theory of gases: gas atoms are perfectly elastic spheres moving in straight lines at constant speed, the pressure is proportional to nmc²/v, and taking the atom's vis viva mc² as the absolute temperature gives the laws of Mariotte and Gay-Lussac and equal numbers of atoms in equal volumes. The German original is under each paragraph.
- Status: Peirce ("Evolutionary Love", 1893, ¶20) mentions "notable memoirs by Clausius and Krönig" in 1856 but gives no titles; Claude chose this paper for Krönig. There is no transcription; the text was built from the OCR and checked against all 8 page images of the Internet Archive scan. The translation is by Claude (AI) and has not been reviewed by a person. Quote and cite the original.
### ウィリアム・ジェームズの「I と Me」を、原典で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/william-james-self-ja.html
- One-line: A reading guide to William James's writings on the self and consciousness (Psychology: Briefer Course, 1892, ch.12; The Principles of Psychology, 1890, ch.9 and ch.10; The Varieties of Religious Experience, 1902; "Does 'Consciousness' Exist?", 1904; all public domain), listed in reading order with where to open each (Internet Archive page links and the York University full texts), and under each, key sentences in the English original with a Japanese translation and page numbers: the I (the self as knower) and the Me (the self as known) as "discriminated aspects" and not separate things, the warmth and intimacy of what belongs to one's own self, the passing Thought as the only verifiable thinker, the stream of thought and its fringe, mystical states, and consciousness as a function (knowing) rather than an entity.
- Status: Key sentences only, chosen by Claude; pages were checked against the scans. Later research (Gallagher & Zahavi in the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy; Guillot 2017) and Mead's "I" and "me" (1934) are given as links and summaries without translation. Not to be confused with the page on Henry James Sr.'s Substance and Shadow (William's father). The translation is by Claude (AI) and has not been reviewed by a person. Quote and cite the original.
### ジェームズに辿り着くまで
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/to-james.html
- One-line: A diary-like record of one "aha" moment by pjdhiro (subtitle: "the warm feeling of I, and a dry breathing sound"): having taken the English I and me as mere grammar, he went through four experiences (seeing an object as "that" in object-oriented programming; in shikan meditation, what he had taken as I separating into me; on waking, hearing a dry breathing sound with no me present) and noticed that he lives as a composite of I and me. Each chapter adds one checked passage from William James, read only after the experience (Briefer Course 1892 p.176; Principles 1890 pp.291, 331, 333, 341, 400–401; "Does 'Consciousness' Exist?" 1904 p.491, "I breathe").
- Status: A single, naive first-person experience (N=1), not an argument; James is used as a footing, not as proof. In pjdhiro's felt sense the warmth is on the side of I and the me side felt dry, which differs in direction from James's "warmth and intimacy" of what belongs to one's self; the page leaves the difference as it is. Translations are by Claude (AI).
### 聞こえていなかった呼吸の音
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/breath-filter.html
- One-line: A short page (subtitle: "the filter on signals rising to consciousness, and me") that starts from pjdhiro's experience of hearing his own breathing as a dry sound on waking, with no "me" present, and his provisional conclusion that "the correction of hearing had stopped". It goes through where one's own breathing sound is normally turned down: in the ear (the normally closed Eustachian tube keeps the energy of one's own voice and breathing away from the middle ear; in patulous Eustachian tube one hears one's own breathing, Bance et al. 2019), in the brain's anticipation of the results of one's own movements (self-tickling, Blakemore et al. 1998; self-triggered sounds, Martikainen et al. 2005; own speech, Ventura et al. 2009; corollary discharge, Crapse & Sommer 2008; precision, Brown et al. 2013), and in what reaches consciousness (Hohwy 2012; Herrero et al. 2018; Barrett & Simmons 2015; Seth 2013). It then links this to James's "the nucleus of the 'me' is always the bodily existence felt to be present at the time" (1890, p.400) and to the interoceptive model of presence and depersonalization (Seth, Suzuki & Critchley 2012), and puts forward the hypothesis that one stopped correction may account both for hearing the breath and for the absence of me.
- Status: A single, naive first-person experience (N=1) and a hypothesis, not an argument. All sources were checked in their full text; none of them measured the sound of breathing itself, so applying them to breathing is the page's hypothesis. The research describes sub-second brain processes that are not felt; the experience is what was felt. Medical descriptions are not a diagnosis. Translations are by Claude (AI).

### クラウジウス「熱と呼ぶ運動の種類について」（1857）を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/clausius-art-der-bewegung-ja.html
- One-line: A full Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of Rudolf Clausius's paper "Ueber die Art der Bewegung, welche wir Wärme nennen" (Annalen der Physik und Chemie 100, 1857, pp.353–380; public domain; German), his first paper on the kinetic theory of gases: besides the translational motion of the molecules (as in Krönig), the parts of each molecule rotate and vibrate, and their vis viva is also heat; he explains why the gas laws hold only approximately, the states of aggregation, evaporation and the volumes of combining gases, derives p = nmu²/3v, the speed of the molecules (about 461 m/s for oxygen at freezing point) and the ratio K/H = 3/2 (c'/c − 1) of the translational vis viva to the whole heat. The German original is under each paragraph.
- Status: Peirce ("Evolutionary Love", 1893, ¶20) mentions "notable memoirs by Clausius and Krönig" in 1856 but gives no titles; Claude chose this paper for Clausius (it is dated January 1857). There is no transcription; the text was built from the OCR and checked against all 28 page images of the Internet Archive scan. The translation is by Claude (AI) and has not been reviewed by a person. Quote and cite the original.

### マクスウェル「気体の動力学的理論の例解」（1860）を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/maxwell-dynamical-theory-of-gases-ja.html
- One-line: A full Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of James Clerk Maxwell's paper "Illustrations of the Dynamical Theory of Gases" (Philosophical Magazine, 4th ser., vol. 19, 1860, pp.19–32 and vol. 20, 1860, pp.21–37; Parts I–III; public domain; English), read at the British Association at Aberdeen in September 1859: treating a gas as many perfectly elastic spheres in collision, he shows that the velocities are distributed by the same law as errors in the method of least squares (Prop. IV, now the Maxwell distribution), that the mean vis viva of particles of different systems becomes equal, and derives the mean length of path, pressure, internal friction, diffusion and conduction of heat; in Part III the equality of translational and rotational vis viva for non-spherical bodies contradicts the known ratio of specific heats (1.408). The English original is under each paragraph.
- Status: Peirce ("Evolutionary Love", 1893, ¶20) says that "in the very summer preceding Darwin's publication, Maxwell had read before the British Association the first and most important of his researches on this subject" without a title; this is that research. There is no transcription; the text was built from the OCR and checked against all 31 page images of the Internet Archive scans. The translation is by Claude (AI) and has not been reviewed by a person. Quote and cite the original.

### バックル『イギリス文明史』（1857）の、統計が示す規則性の所を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/buckle-history-of-civilization-ja.html
- One-line: A Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of pages 18–33 of Chapter I of Henry Thomas Buckle's History of Civilization in England, vol. 1 (London: John W. Parker and Son, 1857; public domain; English), where Buckle rejects the dogmas of free will and predestination and argues from statistics (murders, suicides, marriages and the price of corn, letters posted without an address) that human actions, taken in the aggregate of a society, recur with a regularity like that of physical laws.
- Status: only Chapter I, pp.18–33 (17 paragraphs and footnotes 19–37) is translated; Peirce ("Evolutionary Love", 1893, ¶20) says the first volume "had created a tremendous sensation, owing to the use he made of this same idea" (the idea that chance begets order) but names no chapter or page, and Claude chose this passage. There is no transcription of the first edition; the text was built from the OCR and checked against the page images of the Internet Archive scan (10278775bsb). The statistical works Buckle cites were not checked. The translation is by Claude (AI) and has not been reviewed by a person.

### ケトレー『確率論についての書簡』（1846）の、平均と誤差の所を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/quetelet-lettres-probabilites-ja.html
- One-line: A Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of seven letters from Adolphe Quetelet's Lettres sur la théorie des probabilités, appliquée aux sciences morales et politiques (Brussels: M. Hayez, 1846; public domain; French): Letters XVII–XXII on the theory of means (repeated measurements fall about the mean not at random but in the order given by the scale of possibility), the probable error and the scale of precision, an astronomical example (Greenwich observations of the right ascension of the pole star), the chest measurements of 5738 Scottish soldiers and the heights of French conscripts as evidence of a human type (the average man), and ordinary and extraordinary events (giants and dwarfs); and Letter XXX on variable causes that may be treated as constant and the law of large numbers, which Quetelet calls the first mathematical proof that an average man really exists.
- Status: only Letters XVII–XXII (pp.113–156) and XXX (pp.213–216) are translated (119 paragraphs and 2 footnotes); the endnotes are not. Peirce ("Evolutionary Love", 1893, ¶20) says Quetelet "had opened the discussion" of the idea that chance begets order with these Letters but names no letter; the letters were chosen with pjdhiro from three options. The text was read from the page images of the Internet Archive scan (lettressarleduc00quetgoog), and the tables were checked by calculation; printer's errors are kept and noted. The translation is by Claude (AI) and has not been reviewed by a person.

### ドレイパー『ヨーロッパの知的発展の歴史』（1863）の第 10 章「東方の信仰の時代」を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/draper-intellectual-development-ja.html
- One-line: A Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of Chapter X ("The European Age of Faith: Age of Faith in the East") of John William Draper's History of the Intellectual Development of Europe (New York: Harper, 1863; public domain; English), which tells how, after Constantine, Christianity was paganized in alliance with the state, how Patristicism (the science of the Fathers) held that the sacred writings contained all that man needs to know and pushed aside Greek learning, how under Theodosius the Archbishop Theophilus pillaged the library of the Serapion at Alexandria and razed the temple, and how under his nephew Cyril the philosopher Hypatia was murdered and Alexandrian science suppressed.
- Status: the whole of Chapter X (25 paragraphs, with the chapter summary from the table of contents and the 33 marginal notes) is translated; Peirce ("Evolutionary Love", 1893, ¶35, note 63) names this chapter for the destruction of the great library of Alexandria by Theophilus. The fourth edition (1866) slightly revises the wording, so the first-edition text was translated; no open scan of the 1863 New York printing was found, and the text was read from the page images of the London printing of the same text (Bell and Daldy, 1864, vol. 1, pp.298–315; Internet Archive bub_gb_lsdyKsjXFkkC). The history Draper gives and the passages he quotes were not checked. The translation is by Claude (AI) and has not been reviewed by a person.

### トムソン「熱」（『ブリタニカ百科事典』第 9 版・1880）を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/thomson-heat-ja.html
- One-line: A Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of the whole article "Heat" by William Thomson (later Lord Kelvin) in the Encyclopaedia Britannica, 9th edition, vol. XI (Edinburgh: A. & C. Black, 1880, pp.554–589; public domain; English): the sense of heat and latent heat, calorimetry, the nature of heat as motion and Joule's dynamical equivalent of heat, thermometers and the absolute thermodynamic scale of temperature (with an estimate of absolute zero), the conduction, radiation and diffusivity of heat, tables of thermal properties, and a mathematical appendix on solutions of the equation of the transference of heat.
- Status: the whole article (212 paragraphs and 50 footnotes, with tables I–X and appendix I–XVII) is translated. Peirce ("Evolutionary Love", 1893, note 64) says that Thomson in this article never once mentions the name of Clausius; read in full against the page images, the name appears four times (a marginal note on entropy, p.570; the text of §76 on the thermal conductivity of gases, p.579; the authority column of Tables VIII and IX, p.586), but not in §§8–9, which tell the history of the theory that heat is motion. The text was read from the page images of the Internet Archive scan (in.ernet.dli.2015.208654); formulas were checked by calculation and printer's errors are kept and noted. The translation is by Claude (AI) and has not been reviewed by a person.

### ヘラパス『数理物理学』（1847）の、気体の運動論の所を、日本語で読む
- URL: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/reader/herapath-mathematical-physics-ja.html
- One-line: A Japanese translation, paragraph by paragraph, of the passages on the kinetic theory of gases in John Herapath's Mathematical Physics, vol. 1 (London: Whittaker, 1847; public domain; English), where Herapath treats a gas as small particles moving about in a vessel and striking one another and its sides, derives gaseous elasticity (pressure) from their impacts, takes heat to be the intestine motion of the particles and temperature its degree, and from definitions and propositions obtains the laws of expansion and contraction of gases, a point of absolute cold, and relations among the number, mass and velocity of the particles.
- Status: three passages are translated (Book I §9–§10, pp.12–17; Book II §40–§46, pp.212–220; Book II Sect. II "Of the Laws of Gaseous Bodies", pp.236–265; 146 paragraphs). Peirce ("Evolutionary Love", 1893, ¶20) says Herapath "had in 1847 outlined the kinetical theory of gases in his 'Mathematical Physics'" but names no chapter or page; the theory is spread over these three places, and all three were chosen with pjdhiro. Volume 1 has no transcription and no Internet Archive scan; the text was read from the page images of the Harvard copy on Google Books (id=nH0tAAAAYAAJ), and the formulas were checked by calculation. The experimental works Herapath cites were not checked. The translation is by Claude (AI) and has not been reviewed by a person.
